title: Could Political Stability Spoil The Spanish Debt Miracle?

Could Political Stability Spoil The Spanish Debt Miracle?

Cedric Gemehl

Gavekal Research | 19 Nov 2026

Spain has achieved something unusual in Europe: a spectacular reduction in public debt despite political paralysis and little fiscal consolidation. As Spaniards head to the polls on November 29, investors will be wondering whether a change of government could derail this progress. Probably not, although greater political stability could paradoxically slow the decline in debt by allowing more fiscal slippage than continued gridlock.Spain’s public debt has fallen from a peak of 119% of GDP during the 2020 pandemic to 101% in 2025. The Spanish finance ministry expects it to decline further to 99.1% in 2026 and 92.8% by 2030. This remarkable performance has come despite two developments that have complicated the country’s fiscal position: higher interest rates and political fragmentation.
